title: The Famished Khalsa Looks Toward Treacherous Hill Allies

blocks.text: By now the Khalsa is near collapse from constant flight. Food and water failed, horses are worn down, and day and night march has left the Singhs with little chance to camp, cook, or tend their wounded before the next movement becomes necessary.

Their equipment is failing as badly as their bodies. Broken bows, blunted weapons, and famished mounts show that the campaign is being fought beyond the limits of ordinary endurance, with survival depending more on resolve than on any secure line of supply.

In that condition some hope that the hill chiefs or nearby Hindu households might offer relief, but the narrative prepares the reader for betrayal rather than sanctuary. The same hill interests that had abandoned Banda Singh Bahadur are about to fail the Khalsa again, turning desperate trust into another snare.
